title: LIVE CLOUD COVER — North America Coverage
freshness: LIVE / CURRENT OBSERVATION + MODEL FILL (GOES FD 10-min + RRFS/GDPS fallback)
noaa_source: NOAA GOES-East (GOES-19) + GOES-West (GOES-18) ABI L2 Clear Sky Mask full-disk observations, RRFS TCDC fallback, GDPS fallback
product_name: NOAA GOES-East (GOES-19) + GOES-West (GOES-18) ABI L2 Clear Sky Mask full-disk observations, RRFS TCDC fallback, GDPS fallback
variable: BCM binary mask (0=clear_or_probably_clear, 1=cloudy_or_probably_cloudy) gated DQF==0 -> % per canvas neighborhood; model TCDC % in fallback domain
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: GOES BCM/DQF==0 valid > RRFS TCDC > GDPS (verified gaps) > transparent; missing never 0%.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.
attribution: Data: US NOAA. This project is not endorsed by NOAA. See DATA_SOURCES.md for exact products and endpoints.
legend_scale_html: Cloud cover (%, OBSERVED neighborhood fraction from GOES: share of 2 km satellite pixels flagged cloudy around each point): LOWEST 0 clear transparent → thin cloud dark-blue/blue/cyan → 40 green → 55 yellow → 70 orange → 82 red → 90 magenta → HIGHEST+ 100 overcast dark-purple. Same % always shows the same color; clear areas stay see-through. Satellite retrieval where GOES is valid, model fill elsewhere (see provenance).

na_bounds.note: Authoritative common geography for the four North American live layers (precipitation_na, air_temperature_na, cloud_cover_na, wind_na). Every NA builder bins its own source grid onto this exact canvas, so the four overlays align in Google Earth. Degrees per pixel: 0.05 x 0.05 (square). This boundary is a bounding extent enclosing the buffered landmass; it does not imply valid source data everywhere — areas without valid source data stay transparent.
